newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters admits tough start for coalition.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters admits tough start for coalition.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters said on Wednesday that the centre-right coalition government had encountered difficulties in its first 100 days in office but was delivering substantial gains.
"Yes, we have had our little challenges that have grabbed the headlines in recent times," Peters told a business audience in his home electorate of Tauranga.

Peters, who leads junior coalition partner New Zealand First, acknowledged the "unsettling impact" of a controversy over funding of a Maori television station in which one of his party's MPs has been embroiled.

He also alluded to his recent heated altercation in a corridor of parliament with another government MP, John Banks. Parliament's privileges committee is examining an allegation, denied by Peters, that he assaulted Banks.
Peters said publicity over the incident had been "negative and unfortunate", and opponents had been "grandstanding for political gain".
"No one said this early phase would be easy, yet despite the occasional sensational headline, the coalition is working well, and substantial gains are being made," Peters said.
He said the government's planned injection of NZ$5 billion of extra spending over three years was affordable and would made a substantial impact.
Peters said he was confident the next 900 days would be "even more productive, though a little less colourful".
